fullPassage:
"Millennials Are Not Getting Married!" and "How to Deal with Generation MZ in the Workplace" are some newspaper headlines that have been featured in recent years. The Gen MZ concept is everywhere and is often used to frame a generational conflict or explain a social phenomenon. Can a generation-based approach help solve our social issues? And to what extent can our generation labels define who we are, or predict our behavior?
Sociologists classify generations based on an individual's birth year. The four most recent generations are baby boomers, Generation X, Generation Y (or millennials), and Generation Z. Baby boomers are named so because the birth rate was significantly higher when they were born. But since Korea and the U.S. experienced dramatic population increases during different periods, their classifications of baby boomers differ accordingly. In the U.S., baby boomers are people born between 1946 and 1964, but in Korea, baby boomers are those born between 1955 and 1963. Generation X (1965-1980) earned its name from the title of a book written by Douglas Coupland in 1991. According to the book, people in their twenties in that era had a relaxed and laid-back lifestyle. The following generations, born after Generation X, were later called Y (1981-1996) and Z (1997-2012). Members of Generation Y are also called millennials because they became adults with the beginning of the new millennium.
The cohort effect and the traditional notion of a generation are closely related. Broadly speaking, each generation is defined by the birth years of its members. According to the theory of generational cohorts, individuals who belong to a particular generation are socialized in distinct conditions compared to other generations. They experience similar political, economic, and social events during their early stages of life, which shape their beliefs, values, and behaviors in similar ways.
The cohort effect results in characteristic differences between generations. For instance, Koreans went through the 1997 financial crisis, also known as the International Monetary Fund (IMF) crisis. Gen Xers were in their 20s at that time, and thus experienced great employment instability. This may have led them to prioritize secure employment for their children. In contrast, Gen Zers grew up with smartphones, and this earned them the "digital natives" label. They are accustomed to getting their news, information, and advice from social media. Their strength in using digital media, however, often leads them to lack social skills.
Do Gen Xers only care about job stability while Gen Zers are entirely selfish? Such simple classifications as this rarely prove to be accurate. The life cycle effect suggests that major life events, such as leaving home, separating from parents, getting married, or having children, can alter people's values and attitudes. Many individuals say they used to be more adventurous and drawn to liberal lifestyles during their youth. But they tend to become more responsible after getting married and take fewer risks after having children.
A case in point is the assessment of millennials in the workplace. In the early 2000s, when this group initially entered the job market, they were perceived as being less committed to their companies. However, as they aged and got used to their roles, they began to be increasingly recognized as diligent workers. This illustrates that the pursuit of freedom is more characteristic of youth than of a specific generation, as certain attitudes and behaviors naturally develop during different life stages.
Apart from when a person is born or which life stage they are going through, some radical changes, like the climate crisis, affect all age groups. According to some U.S. survey results, there was no significant age divide in recognizing the importance of climate change around the world. Nearly half of each generation responded that the rise in world temperature is very dangerous. Another survey conducted by German researchers showed similar consumption rates of ethical products between older and younger generations. When baby boomers were young, climate change was not such a prominent issue and therefore was not much of a concern. But now, regardless of age, people across different generations are concerned about its effects.
These different perspectives suggest that we should be careful not to make hasty judgments about people according to their generation labels. We don't want to consider only when a person was born. This can lead to overgeneralizations that don't capture all aspects of a person's unique individual identity. We should consider various perspectives, which will help us achieve a better understanding of people regardless of their generation.

questions.passage: Sociologists (A)[classify / distribute] generations based on an individual's birth year. Baby boomers are named so because the birth rate was (B)[significantly / significant] higher when they were born. According to the theory of generational cohorts, individuals who belong to a particular generation are socialized in (C)[distinct / vague] conditions compared to other generations.
questions.stem: (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 사회학자들은 세대를 분류한다(classify). 출생률이 상당히(significantly) 높았다. 뚜렷한(distinct) 조건에서 사회화된다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② classify–significantly–distinct: 모두 원문 적합. significantly는 higher를 수식하는 부사.
❌ ① significant는 형용사라 higher를 수식 불가
❌ ③ distribute(분배하다)는 문맥 부적합, vague(모호한)는 distinct 반의어
❌ ④ 전부 부적합
det.tip: classify(분류하다) ↔ distribute(분배하다) / significantly(부사) vs significant(형용사) / distinct(뚜렷한) ↔ vague(모호한)

questions.passage: Gen Xers were in their 20s at that time, and thus experienced great employment instability. This may have led them to prioritize secure employment for their children. Their (B)[strength / weakness] in using digital media, however, often leads them to (C)[lack / possess] social skills. Do Gen Xers only care about job stability while Gen Zers are entirely selfish?
questions.stem: (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: Z세대는 소셜 미디어에서 뉴스를 얻는 것에 익숙하다(accustomed). 디지털 미디어 사용의 강점(strength)이 오히려 사회적 기술의 부족(lack)으로 이어진다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① accustomed–strength–lack: 모두 원문 그대로 적합
❌ ② weakness는 strength 반의어, possess는 lack 반의어
❌ ③ opposed(반대하는)는 accustomed 반의어
❌ ④ 전부 반의어 조합
det.tip: be accustomed to(~에 익숙한) ↔ be opposed to(~에 반대하는) / strength(강점) ↔ weakness(약점)

❌ ③ accustomed: 원문 그대로 적절

det.analysis:

❌ ① alter: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ② adventurous: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ④ develop: 원문 그대로 적절
det.tip: take risks(위험을 감수하다) ↔ take opportunities(기회를 잡다). 문맥 단서: 'more responsible'과 연결

And to what extent can our generation labels define who we are, or predict our behavior?
Sociologists classify generations based on an individual's birth year. The four most recent generations are baby boomers, Generation X, Generation Y (or millennials), and Generation Z. Baby boomers are named so because the birth rate was significantly higher when they were born. But since Korea and the U.S. experienced dramatic population increases during different periods, their classifications of baby boomers differ accordingly. In the U.S., baby boomers are people born between 1946 and 1964, but in Korea, baby boomers are those born between 1955 and 1963. Generation X (1965-1980) earned its name from the title of a book written by Douglas Coupland in 1991. According to the book, people in their twenties in that era had a relaxed and laid-back lifestyle. The following generations, born after Generation X, were later called Y (1981-1996) and Z (1997-2012). Members of Generation Y are also called millennials because they became adults with the beginning of the new millennium.
The cohort effect and the traditional notion of a generation are closely related. Broadly speaking, each generation is defined by the birth years of its members. According to the theory of generational cohorts, individuals who belong to a particular generation are socialized in distinct conditions compared to other generations. They experience similar political, economic, and social events during their early stages of life, which shape their beliefs, values, and behaviors in similar ways.
The cohort effect results in characteristic differences between generations. For instance, Koreans went through the 1997 financial crisis, also known as the International Monetary Fund (IMF) crisis. Gen Xers were in their 20s at that time, and thus experienced great employment instability. This may have led them to prioritize secure employment for their children. In contrast, Gen Zers grew up with smartphones, and this earned them the "digital natives" label. They are accustomed to getting their news, information, and advice from social media. Their strength in using digital media, however, often leads them to lack social skills.
Do Gen Xers only care about job stability while Gen Zers are entirely selfish? Such simple classifications as this rarely prove to be accurate. The life cycle effect suggests that major life events, such as leaving home, separating from parents, getting married, or having children, can <u>alter</u> people's values and attitudes. Many individuals say they used to be more adventurous and drawn to liberal lifestyles during their youth. But they tend to become more responsible after getting married and take fewer risks after having children.
A case in point is the assessment of millennials in the workplace. In the early 2000s, when this group initially entered the job market, they were perceived as being less committed to their companies. However, as they aged and got used to their roles, they began to be increasingly recognized as diligent workers. This illustrates that the pursuit of freedom is more characteristic of youth than of a specific generation, as certain attitudes and behaviors naturally develop during different life stages.
Apart from when a person is born or which life stage they are going through, some radical changes, like the climate crisis, affect all age groups. According to some U.S. survey results, there was no significant age divide in recognizing the importance of climate change around the world. Nearly half of each generation responded that the rise in world temperature is very dangerous. Another survey conducted by German researchers showed similar consumption rates of ethical products between older and younger generations. When baby boomers were young, climate change was not such a prominent issue and therefore was not much of a concern. But now, regardless of age, people across different generations are concerned about its effects.
These different perspectives suggest that we should be careful not to make hasty judgments about people according to their generation labels. We don't want to consider only when a person was born. This can lead to overgeneralizations that don't capture all aspects of a person's unique individual identity. We should consider various perspectives, which will help us achieve a better understanding of people regardless of their generation.

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A) stages와 (B) overgeneralizations의 문맥적 의미로 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 삶의 초기 단계(stages)에서 유사한 사건을 경험한다. (B) 이것은 개인의 정체성을 포착하지 못하는 과잉 일반화(overgeneralizations)로 이어질 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 단계–일반화: (A) stages는 '생애 단계'의 의미, (B) overgeneralizations는 '과잉 일반화'
❌ ① 세대–접근법: stages를 세대로 해석하면 generations와 중복
❌ ② 단계–접근법: overgeneralizations를 접근법으로 볼 수 없음
❌ ③ 세대–일반화: stages를 세대로 해석 부적합
det.tip: stage = 단계, 시기 / overgeneralization = 과도한 일반화 (over- 접두사 주목)

det.analysis:
✅ ① prioritize: treat as more important = 우선시하다
❌ ② classify(분류하다): 중요도와 무관

det.tip: prioritize = prior(먼저) + -ize(~하다) = 우선순위를 매기다

ch: ignore the effects of climate change
questions.passage:
"Millennials Are Not Getting Married!" and "How to Deal with Generation MZ in the Workplace" are some newspaper headlines that have been featured in recent years. The Gen MZ concept is everywhere and is often used to frame a generational conflict or explain a social phenomenon. Can a generation-based approach help solve our social issues? And to what extent can our generation labels define who we are, or predict our behavior?
Sociologists classify generations based on an individual's birth year. The four most recent generations are baby boomers, Generation X, Generation Y (or millennials), and Generation Z. Baby boomers are named so because the birth rate was significantly higher when they were born. But since Korea and the U.S. experienced dramatic population increases during different periods, their classifications of baby boomers differ accordingly. In the U.S., baby boomers are people born between 1946 and 1964, but in Korea, baby boomers are those born between 1955 and 1963. Generation X (1965-1980) earned its name from the title of a book written by Douglas Coupland in 1991. According to the book, people in their twenties in that era had a relaxed and laid-back lifestyle. The following generations, born after Generation X, were later called Y (1981-1996) and Z (1997-2012). Members of Generation Y are also called millennials because they became adults with the beginning of the new millennium.
The cohort effect and the traditional notion of a generation are closely related. Broadly speaking, each generation is defined by the birth years of its members. According to the theory of generational cohorts, individuals who belong to a particular generation are socialized in distinct conditions compared to other generations. They experience similar political, economic, and social events during their early stages of life, which shape their beliefs, values, and behaviors in similar ways.
The cohort effect results in characteristic differences between generations. For instance, Koreans went through the 1997 financial crisis, also known as the International Monetary Fund (IMF) crisis. Gen Xers were in their 20s at that time, and thus experienced great employment instability. This may have led them to prioritize secure employment for their children. In contrast, Gen Zers grew up with smartphones, and this earned them the "digital natives" label. They are accustomed to getting their news, information, and advice from social media. Their strength in using digital media, however, often leads them to lack social skills.
Do Gen Xers only care about job stability while Gen Zers are entirely selfish? Such simple classifications as this rarely prove to be accurate. The life cycle effect suggests that major life events, such as leaving home, separating from parents, getting married, or having children, can alter people's values and attitudes. Many individuals say they used to be more adventurous and drawn to liberal lifestyles during their youth. But they tend to become more responsible after getting married and take fewer risks after having children.
A case in point is the assessment of millennials in the workplace. In the early 2000s, when this group initially entered the job market, they were perceived as being less committed to their companies. However, as they aged and got used to their roles, they began to be increasingly recognized as diligent workers. This illustrates that the pursuit of freedom is more characteristic of youth than of a specific generation, as certain attitudes and behaviors naturally develop during different life stages.
Apart from when a person is born or which life stage they are going through, some radical changes, like the climate crisis, affect all age groups. According to some U.S. survey results, there was no significant age divide in recognizing the importance of climate change around the world. Nearly half of each generation responded that the rise in world temperature is very dangerous. Another survey conducted by German researchers showed similar consumption rates of ethical products between older and younger generations. When baby boomers were young, climate change was not such a prominent issue and therefore was not much of a concern. But now, regardless of age, people across different generations are concerned about its effects.
These different perspectives suggest that we should be careful not to ____ according to their generation labels. We don't want to consider only when a person was born. This can lead to overgeneralizations that don't capture all aspects of a person's unique individual identity. We should consider various perspectives, which will help us achieve a better understanding of people regardless of their generation.

det.korean: 세대 레이블에 따라 사람들에 대해 성급한 판단을 하지 않도록 주의해야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ make hasty judgments about people: 원문 그대로의 표현.
❌ ① create a new generation label: 글의 요지와 무관
❌ ② predict people's behavior accurately: 정확히 예측하라는 내용 아님
❌ ④ ignore the effects of climate change: 기후변화는 별도 소재
det.tip: make hasty judgments = 성급한 판단을 내리다. 글의 결론: 세대 레이블로 사람을 판단하지 말라
